title: Discretionary trading to trading system - is it possible?
author: Wise_Lion_9703
selftext:
I've been trading less manually lately and trying to automate more of it. There are several reasons why ...

First, I just don't have enough time to watch charts all day, but also because I know my own psychology is probably my biggest weakness. I overthink entries, close winners too early, hold losers too long, get too stressed and emotional ... all the usual stuff. Or I just miss a good entry because I sleep. I do tend to sleep occaionally, how unfortunate.

Feels like traders in the future might spend less time clicking buy and sell, and more time building, testing and improving systems.

I know you're probably experiencing the same but the question is how to translate a discretionary trader to a repeatable system with edge. Because a lot of my trading is just a result of years of trading and knowledge I canot 100% quantify ... which makes me wonder.

Can intuition be quantified and put into a system?

comments.author: UnitedAcanthaceae118
comments.body: Everstrike has a discretionary mode which lets your AI agent use discretion. It may not be as good at making decisions as you but could be something worth looking into.

comments.author: Quant_Nexus
comments.body: In my experience, no. Every time I've met someone with "a working trading system" and I have them write the rules down, they massively fail in backtesting. Not forward testing, backtesting... Which means that they weren't following the rules. Looking at executed trades shows that they don't follow their own rules, which then leads to a bunch of "contingency rules" getting added ("well I bought this set up here since I saw XYZ was also happening") which then gets coded up into a rule... That also fails the backtesting.
